user.title: Connect to your receiver
user.description: Enter the address of your Onkyo, Integra or Pioneer receiver. The eISCP port is normally 60128. These receivers accept only one controller at a time, so disable any other controller (for example Node-RED) before continuing.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the receiver (without a port, for example 10.0.1.209).
data_description.port: TCP port of the receiver. Network (eISCP) receivers normally use 60128.
data_description.protocol: Use Network (eISCP) for the built-in Ethernet port. Use Serial bridge only if the receiver is reached through a serial-to-TCP bridge such as ser2net.
data_description.model: Your receiver model. Only the inputs and listening modes this model supports are offered. Choose Other / not listed to get all known inputs and modes.
data_description.name: Name of the receiver in Home Assistant.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure receiver connection
reconfigure.description: Update the connection settings of your receiver. Make sure no other controller (for example Node-RED) is connected to it.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the receiver (without a port, for example 10.0.1.209).
data_description.port: TCP port of the receiver. Network (eISCP) receivers normally use 60128.
data_description.protocol: Use Network (eISCP) for the built-in Ethernet port. Use Serial bridge only if the receiver is reached through a serial-to-TCP bridge such as ser2net.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the receiver. Check the host and port, and that no other app is using the connection.
error.no_response: Connected, but the receiver did not answer. Check the protocol setting and make sure no other app (for example Node-RED) is connected to it.
error.host_includes_port: Enter only the host here and put the port in the Port field.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

init.title: Receiver model and volume
init.description: Changing the model resets the shown inputs and listening modes to the defaults of that model on the next page.

data_description.model: Your receiver model. Only the inputs and listening modes this model supports are offered.
data_description.volume_resolution: Number of volume steps your receiver supports. Most older receivers use 100 steps; some use 80 or 200.
data_description.max_volume: Upper volume limit as a percentage of the receiver's range. Volume commands from Home Assistant never exceed it.

select.title: Inputs and listening modes
select.description: Choose which inputs and listening modes are shown in Home Assistant. If the receiver switches to a hidden one, Home Assistant still shows its name.

data_description.sources: Inputs shown in the input list. At least one is required.
data_description.sound_modes: Listening modes shown in the listening mode list.

names.title: Input names
names.description: Rename the inputs to match what is connected to them. Leave a field empty to use the standard name shown in the field label.

options.iscp: Serial bridge (raw ISCP over TCP, e.g. ser2net)

cannot_connect.message: Could not connect to the receiver at {host}:{port}.

query_timeout.message: The receiver did not answer the query in time.

unknown_source.message: Unknown source. Choose one of the configured sources.

send_raw_command.name: Send raw command
send_raw_command.description: Sends a raw ISCP command, such as SWL+2, to the receiver.

command.name: Command
command.description: The ISCP command and value to send, without the leading !1.

query.name: Query
query.description: Asks the receiver for the value of a 3-letter command (for example MVL) and returns the answer.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long to wait for the answer, in seconds.
